items.name: Readability
items.evidence: Names are clear and the formatting matches the file. But `json.dumps(str(final_key))` has no comment saying why the last key is forced to an object key. The rewritten KeyTransformIsNull no longer uses HasKey and has no comment explaining why.

items.name: Maintainability
items.evidence: There is no overridable hook or HasKeyOrArrayIndex subclass. KeyTransformIsNull copies the SQL templates (`"JSON_EXISTS(%s, '%s')"`, `JSON_TYPE` with a manual path) instead of reusing HasKey. KeyTransformExact.as_oracle still uses HasKey, so the two callers now work differently.

items.name: Robustness
items.evidence: This is a small SQL-building change with no exceptions or resources to handle. `str(final_key)` safely handles int keys. Params are threaded through correctly, including `tuple(lhs_params) * 2`. No magic constants and no swallowed errors.

items.name: Array-index semantics kept for isnull / exact=None paths
items.name_zh: isnull / exact=None 路径保留数组下标语义
items.evidence: The has_key family is fixed in the shared `as_sql` for all three backends, and KeyTransformIsNull keeps array-index semantics through `compile_json_path(lhs_key_transforms)`. But KeyTransformExact.as_oracle still calls `HasKey(self.lhs.lhs, self.lhs.key_name)`, so on Oracle `value__d__0=None` now treats 0 as an object key.
